body:
Build a complete **Bloxwap-owned human interface guideline and component system** that every Bloxwap repository can apply to React web and React Native mobile interfaces, documentation, and marketing surfaces.

## Product direction

- Carry forward our existing web/mobile component design, Bloxwap Sans/Mono/Pixel fonts, brand palette and marks, geometry, and interactions. Start from evidence in current products and SDK docs.
- Use small composable components, shared tokens/behavioral contracts, and separate DOM/native renderers. Consolidate duplication while preserving intentional touch-app versus compact-Pro differences.
- Compose visual state and motion with optional Bloxwap SFX and haptic adapters. Support sound only, haptics only, both, neither, and host-owned adapters without changing the primary action.
- Prefer versioned packages with individual imports to repeated source copies; finalize names/primitive choices in the architecture task. Arbitrary shadcn compatibility, its full component catalog, a universal theme generator, and a shadcn registry/CLI are outside v1.
- Make the landing page a configuration-panel plus live-preview playground inspired by [shadcn Create](https://ui.shadcn.com/create), with Bloxwap-approved choices. Shape the catalog and component pages after [shadcn component docs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components).

## Starting evidence and integration constraints

The monorepo already has [shared tokens](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/packages/tokens), [shared web primitives](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/packages/ui), [app-owned primitives](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/apps/app/src/components/ui), [Pro controls](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/apps/pro/src/components/ui), [native primitives](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/packages/ui-native), and [plain CSS/UI](https://github.com/bloxwap/monorepo/tree/main/packages/plain-ui). The audit must identify ownership and legitimate differences before extraction.

[@bloxwap/font](https://github.com/bloxwap/font/blob/main/packages/npm/README.md) provides Sans, Mono, Pixel, and script companions. Native typography requires explicit asset registration and scale mapping. Existing token docs identify web/native rem-root and color-space differences that must be preserved or changed deliberately.

The [SFX native guide](https://github.com/bloxwap/sfx/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/guides/native.mdx) provides offline WAV export for native playback. The [haptic platform guide](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/blob/main/apps/docs/content/docs/platforms.mdx) describes a React/web implementation with physical-tap iOS and browser-vibration constraints; HIG must implement an explicit RN haptics adapter. Physical-device certification is tracked upstream in [bloxwap/haptic#9](https://github.com/bloxwap/haptic/issues/9). API calls and simulator tests are not evidence of tactile output.

## Execution

All 35 tasks are required for v1. **P0** marks foundational work and the first usable integrations; **P1** completes catalog coverage, guidance, and rollout. Follow each issue's direct prerequisites. Milestones group deliverables; component, feedback, docs, and quality work can proceed concurrently once their prerequisites are available.

### M1: Foundations and architecture

Audit existing Bloxwap designs; define HIG principles, architecture, tokens, fonts, layout, motion, accessibility, and brand assets.

- [ ] #2 — Inventory existing Bloxwap interfaces and define the v1 component catalog
- [ ] #3 — Write the Bloxwap HIG principles and product interaction rules
- [ ] #4 — Choose the shared package architecture and source-of-truth ownership
- [ ] #5 — Bootstrap the HIG workspace and runnable web/native consumer fixtures
- [ ] #6 — Extract semantic design tokens and generate web/native color outputs
- [ ] #7 — Integrate Bloxwap fonts and define cross-platform typography
- [ ] #8 — Define spacing, geometry, density, and adaptive layout rules
- [ ] #9 — Specify motion and gesture behavior with reduced-motion alternatives
- [ ] #10 — Establish accessibility, localization, and platform behavior standards
- [ ] #11 — Standardize Bloxwap brand marks and icon usage across web/native

### M2: React and React Native components

Implement the Bloxwap component contracts with React DOM and React Native renderers, platform behavior, chart integration, and product recipes.

- [ ] #12 — Implement shared component contracts and platform providers
- [ ] #13 — Build Bloxwap action and surface primitives for React and RN
- [ ] #14 — Build text input and form-field primitives for React and RN
- [ ] #15 — Build selection, toggle, range, and segmented controls for React and RN
- [ ] #16 — Build dialogs, sheets, menus, and contextual overlays for React and RN
- [ ] #17 — Build navigation, discovery, and disclosure components
- [ ] #18 — Build status, notification, loading, and empty-state components
- [ ] #19 — Build structured data and financial display components
- [ ] #20 — Define chart theming and integrate @bloxwap/chart as an optional component
- [ ] #26 — Build Bloxwap product, marketing, and SDK documentation recipes

### M3: SFX and haptics

Compose semantic interaction feedback with existing Bloxwap SFX and haptic packages and explicit native adapters; support preferences and device verification.

- [ ] #21 — Define the composable sound and haptic feedback contract
- [ ] #22 — Integrate @bloxwap/sfx and @bloxwap/haptic with React web components
- [ ] #23 — Build the React Native SFX asset pipeline and playback adapter
- [ ] #24 — Build the React Native haptics adapter and platform capability matrix
- [ ] #25 — Implement semantic feedback presets, preference controls, and preview recipes

### M4: HIG website and documentation

Build the Bloxwap playground landing page, component catalog, React/React Native previews, and complete human interface guideline documentation.

- [ ] #27 — Build the Bloxwap HIG documentation shell and component catalog
- [ ] #29 — Build the interactive Bloxwap playground landing page
- [ ] #28 — Build component previews, code examples, and a native example gallery
- [ ] #30 — Write the complete HIG, component usage, installation, and migration documentation

### M5: Release and repository adoption

Publish consumable packages, establish quality gates, migrate product and SDK documentation surfaces, and maintain an organization-wide adoption matrix.

- [ ] #32 — Publish versioned HIG packages and automate releases
- [ ] #31 — Add cross-platform quality, accessibility, visual, and size gates
- [ ] #33 — Migrate the Bloxwap app, Pro, and marketing web surfaces to HIG
- [ ] #34 — Migrate Hyperliquid, Chart, Font, SFX, and Haptic documentation to HIG
- [ ] #35 — Migrate the React Native application to HIG and verify iOS/Android behavior
- [ ] #36 — Complete organization-wide adoption and establish HIG governance

## v1 completion criteria

- [ ] The audited component catalog and all foundational HIG chapters are complete, with no orphaned component or unplanned platform gap.
- [ ] React DOM and RN have actual supported implementations/native alternatives, a versioned platform matrix, and passing clean consumer builds.
- [ ] Brand tokens, fonts, icons, units, native color spaces, density, motion, accessibility, and locale behavior are consistent and traceable to one source.
- [ ] Optional sound/haptic composition honors user preferences, event cancellation, unsupported hardware, and deduplication; iOS/Android device evidence matches support claims.
- [ ] Landing playground, component docs, examples/API references, and installation/migration guides work with the shipped artifacts and code examples.
- [ ] Versioned packages/releases and meaningful web/native/SSR/Metro/visual/accessibility/size gates are in place; duplicated source/assets and consumer footprint improvements are measured.
- [ ] bloxwap.app, bloxwap.pro, bloxwap.com, the RN app, and Hyperliquid/Chart/Font/SFX/Haptic docs have migrated surfaces and linked validation.
- [ ] Every active Bloxwap repository has an applicability/adoption decision and migration status, with owners and dated exceptions where needed; governance prevents new design drift.
